text:
maria: quick RFC follow-up: proposing a lightweight tenant-edge adapter pattern. adapter runs ephemeral in customer VPC (or as hosted transient), terminates TLS, issues short session creds, forwards to our regional ingress. goal: avoid permanent peering/ENI per tenant.

sam: high-level differences vs peering: no static routes, adapters are short-lived, less IP/carveouts. default path will SNAT through regional pool unless customer opts into preserve-mode.

ken: preserve-mode = pinned small elastic pool (billed). otherwise lose original source IP. is that acceptable for most customers?

maria: for most yes. offer preserve-mode for enterprise/regulatory.

ravi: cert handling options?

maria: two modes: managed certs (we store keys in KMS, push to adapter with short rotation) or passthrough to tenant backend (requires private endpoint). recommend managed for alpha.

sam: failure/reconnect: adapters stateless; session metadata in CP store (DDB). clients reconnect and present session token for resume within short window (30-120s).

ken: adapters might cache small LLM prefixes to reduce tokens upstream. big caution: cache invalidation and TTLs must be strict.

maria: security: adapters talk over dedicated regional peering. CP must isolate tenant sessions before they reach serving plane. propose route filters + ingress isolation layer.

infra-bot: canary deploy scheduled for us-west-2 at 3370001300 for adapter-prototype.

ravi: ops checklist for pilot: feature-flag, 10 alpha tenants, telemetry (adapter-latency, session-resume-rate, cache-hit-rate), per-adapter rate limits, CP-toggle rollback.

sam: summary: + faster onboarding, smaller long-lived network footprint, easier cert rotation. - loses source-IP by default, needs resume plumbing, adds caching correctness surface.

maria: thanks all 4c5 will follow up with a short spike doc (sequence diagrams + health story). sync tomorrow 9am to pick alphas.
